How to Understand It

Meaning of Each Hygiene Predicate:

  • FV(𝛂) (Free Variables): The set/collection of syntactic variables occurring free in formula or expression 𝛂.
  • NFV(e, x) / Fresh(x, 𝛂) (Not Free Variable / Freshness): Asserts that variable x does not occur free in e (or 𝛂). Crucial in Class Comprehension (Entry 3.02 / 4.01) to prevent circular Russell-style capture where the defined class variable occurs free in its own defining formula, and in Universal Generalisation (Entry 2.03 / 4.02) to verify x ∉ FV(𝒞).
  • FFI(t, x, 𝛂) (Free For In / Capture-Avoiding Substitutability): Asserts that term t is free for variable x in formula 𝛂 (no free variable of t becomes captured by a binder in 𝛂 when substituting t for free occurrences of x). Used in Entries 2.02, 2.05, and 4.03–4.06.
Canonical Law / Usage FFI(t, x, 𝛂) ⇒ ((∀x:Class. 𝛂) ⇒ (let x ↤ t in 𝛂))
